kikata: Kiṃ kata(ti) [kiṃ+kata]  What should be done.
kikaṇikā: Kiṃ kaṇikā(thī) [kaṇa+kika+ā. Kiṃkaṇikādayo saddā kikantā nipaccante. Kaṇa-iti daṇḍakodhātu saddattho, kassa dvittaṃ, assa ittaṃ, niggahītāgamo ca. Moga, 7. 22.] The bell. (It is tinkling bell in Mogasya. It is small bells in Rvheumaṅasya).
kikirāta: [Kiṃ kirāta(pu) [kiṃ+kira+āta. Kiravikkiraṇe, āto, dvittaṃ. Dhāna, ṭī. 579.(kiṅkira+ata+ṇa-saṃ)] A thorny shrub (plant) (Barleria prionitis). (2) Parrot. (3) A tamarind tree (bearing red flowers). (4) Kāma Deva. (5) Cuckoo (bird).
kikirātapuppha: [Kiṃ kirātapuppha(na) [kiṃ kirāta+puppha] Flower of a thorny shrub (plant) (Barleria prionitis).
kikusalagavesī: Kiṃ kusalagavesī(ti) [kiṃ kusala+gavesī] One who is seeking what is good. One who is looking for what is beneficial.
kikusalānuesī: Kiṃ kusalānuesī(ti) [kiṃ kusala+anu+esa+ṇī] One who is looking for omniscience.
kikāra: Kiṃ kāra(pu) [kiṃ+kāra] What should do or service. See - Kiṃ kārapaṭissāvī.
kikārapaṭissāvī: [Kiṃ kārapaṭissāvī(ti) [kiṃkāra+paṭissāvī. In Thī kiṃ kārapaṭissāvinī. "kiṃkaromi sāmī"ti evaṃ kinti kāro karaṇaṃ saddanicchāraṇaṃ kiṃkāro, taṃpaṭissāvetīti kiṃ kārapaṭissāvinī. Nīti, pada. 372.] (A slave) who is speaking what do you want what service (to somebody).
kikārappaṭissāvī: [Kiṃ kārapaṭissāvī(ti) [kiṃkāra+paṭissāvī. In Thī kiṃ kārapaṭissāvinī. "kiṃkaromi sāmī"ti evaṃ kinti kāro karaṇaṃ saddanicchāraṇaṃ kiṃkāro, taṃpaṭissāvetīti kiṃ kārapaṭissāvinī. Nīti, pada. 372.] (A slave) who is speaking what do you want what service (to somebody).
kilakkhaṇa: Kiṃ lakkhaṇa(ti) [kiṃ+lakkhaṇa] Do you have which recognized sign?
kimūlaka: Kiṃ mūlaka(ti) [kiṃ+mūla+ka] Which is the root cause.
kinidāna: Kiṃ nidāna(ti) [kiṃ+nidāna] Have what origin or have what background story.
kininna: Kiṃ ninna (ti) [kiṃ+ninna] Inclining to which or bowed down to what matter or action.
kinu: Kiṃ nu(bya) [kiṃ+nu. Kacci nu kinnu nanu kathaṃ kiṃ su kiṃ iccete pucchanatthe. Rū. Nhā-134.] How? What? Why?
kināma: [Kiṃ nāma(ti) [kiṃ+nāma. Konāmo puriso, kiṃ nāmo vā. Konā mā itthī, kiṃ nāmā vā. Konāmaṃ kulaṃ, kiṃ nāmaṃ vā. Nīti, sutta. 459.]  What is his name?
kiogadha: Kiṃ ogadha(ti) [kiṃ+ogadha]  Observed in what or Focused on what or inclined to where.
kipabbhāra: K ပ ပ ပa ဘာbh ရra (ti) [K + + + + ဗ္ ဘာbh ရra] How deep. Kin Ninna: Look.
kipabhava: Kiṃ pabhava (ti) [kiṃ+pabhava]  Coming from where or coming into being from where. See - Kiṃ jātika.
kipabhutika: Kiṃ pabhutika(ti) [kiṃ+pabhuti+ka] Coming from where. See - Kiṃ pahotika.
kipaccaya: Kiṃ paccaya(pu) [kiṃ+paccaya] What cause or which reason.
kipahotika: Kiṃ pahotika(ti) [kiṃ+pahoti+ka] Coming into being from where or coming from where.
kipakka: Kiṃ pakka(pu) [kiṃ+pakka] A poison fruit. It is a strange fruit that is hard to know in Pītīakaca. See also - Kiṃ pakkarukkha.
kipakkaphala: Kiṃ pakkaphala (na) [kiṃpakka+phala]  A poisonous fruit. See - Kiṃ pakka.
kipakkaphalaparibhoga: [Kiṃ pakkaphalaparibhoga (pu) [kiṃ pakkaphala+paribhoga] Eating the poisoned fruit or decayed fruit.
kipakkarukkha: Kiṃ pakkarukkha(pu) [kiṃ pakka+rukkha] A poisoned tree or a tree that has power to do harm.
kipakāra: Kiṃ pakāra(pu) [kiṃ+pakāra] What method or which way?
kipamukha: Kiṃ pamukha(ti) [kiṃ+pamukha] That is headed by what.
kipariyosāna: Kiṃ pariyosāna(na) [kiṃ+pariyosāna] What is the end?
kipaṭibhāga: Kiṃ paṭibhāga(pu) [kiṃ+paṭibhāga] What nature of things or what state of affairs?
kiphala: Kiṃ phala(ti) [kiṃ+phala] That has what benefit or fruit.
kiphassa: [Kiṃ Phassa (ti) [kiṃ+phassa] One who has what experience.
kipoṇa: [Kiṃ poṇa(ti) [kiṃ+poṇa] Inclines to where or focuses on which. See - Kiṃ ninna.
kipurisa: Kiṃ purisa(pu) [kiṃ+purisa. Assamukhanarasarīratāya kucchito puriso, kiñci vā puriso, purisasadisoti vā kimpuriso. Dhāna, ṭī. 44.] A creature is like people. Kinnarā. See also - Kinnara. Kiṃ purisa(pu) [kiṃ+purisa. Assamukhanarasarīratāya kucchito puriso kiñcī vā puriso purisasadisoti vā kimpuriso, evaṃ kinnaro. Dhāna, ṭī. 44. In Thī kimpurisī] Mythical creature with the head of a horse and the body of a man.
kirukkhaphala: Kiṃ Rukkhaphala (na) [kiṃ rukkha+phala] A fruit that is bearing from which tree.
kisambhava: Kiṃ Sambhava(ti) [kiṃ+sambhava] What is the root cause or origin?
kisambhāra: Kiṃ sambhāra(ti) [kiṃ+sambhāra] Has which thing or requisite.
kisamudaya: [Kiṃ samudaya(ti) [kiṃ+samudaya. Ka+samudaya+ta. Nīti, sutta. 694. Rū. 333.] What is the origin or cause.
kisamuṭṭhāna: Kiṃ samuṭṭhāna(ti) [kiṃ+samuṭṭhāna] What is the origin or cause.
kisamācāra: Kiṃ samācāra(ti) [kiṃ+samācāra] One who has what character?
kisañña: Kiṃ sañña(ti) [kiṃ+saññā] One who has what kind of perception. See - Kiṃ Phassa.
kisakilesajjhāsaya: [Kiṃ saṃkilesajjhāsaya(ti) [kiṃ saṃkilesa+ajjhāsaya] One who has Kilesā. See - Kīdisajjhāsaya.
kisayojana: Kiṃ saṃyojana(ti) [kiṃ+saṃyojana] One who has things which bind.
kisaṇṭhita: Kiṃ saṇṭhita(ti) [kiṃ+saṇṭhita] Existing with what kind of equivalent.
kisuka: [Kiṃ suka(pu) [kiṃ+suka. "ko ayaṃsuko"ti vimatuppattikarapattakusumatāyakiṃ suko. Dhāna, ṭī. 553.] A timber tree (Erythrina stricta). A coral tree. A parrot tree. A silkcotton tree. A Sal tree.
kisukadassāvī: Kiṃ sukadassāvī(ti) [kiṃsuka+disa+āvī] One who has seen a parrot tree.
kisukadiṭṭhabhātika: Kiṃ sukadiṭṭhabhātika(pu) [kiṃsukadiṭṭha+bhātika] The two brothers who have seen a parrot tree.
kisukapatta: Kiṃ sukapatta(na) [kiṃ suka+patta] A leaf of the parrot tree.
kisukapaṇṇa: Kiṃ sukapaṇṇa(na) [kiṃ suka+paṇṇa] A leaf of the parrot tree.
kisukapotakakanda: Kiṃ sukapotakakanda(pu) [kiṃ sukapotaka+kanda] A small bump on the small parrot tree.
kisukapuppha: Kiṃ sukapotakakanda(pu) [kiṃ sukapotaka+kanda] A parrot flower.
kisukapupphavaṇṇa: Kiṃ sukapupphavaṇṇa(ti) [kiṃ sukapuppha+vaṇṇa] One whose appearance is like a parrot flower.
kisukapupphiya: Kiṃ sukapupphiya(pu) [kiṃ suka+puppha+iya] A Thera is named Kiṃ sukapupphiya, who offered the parrot flowers. (A Thera who sees the parrot flowers, offers these flowers aimed at Lord Buddha. For this merit, do not reach the Duggati realms in the whole 31 eons. He became an arahant named Paṭisambhidāpatta chaḷabhiñña at the time of Gotama Lord Buddha).
kisukapūjaka: Kiṃ sukapūjaka(pu) [kiṃ suka+pūjaka]  A Thera is named Kiṃ sukapūjaka, who offered the parrot flowers. (A Thera who sees the parrot flowers, offers these flowers aimed at Lord Buddha Siddhattha who enlightened in the past 94 eons. For this merit, do not reach the Duggati realms in the whole 31 eons. He became an arahant named Paṭisambhidāpatta chaḷabhiñña at the time of Gotama Lord Buddha).
kisukarukkha: Kiṃ sukarukkha(pu) [kiṃ suka+rukkha] A parrot tree. See also - Kiṃsuka.
kisukavallī: Kiṃ sukavallī(thī) [kiṃsuka+vallī] A parrot creeper vine. (There are two kinds of parrot trees, one kind is a tall-stemmed tree and another is a creeper vine).
kisukavana: Kiṃ Sukavana (na) [kiṃ suka+vana] A parrot trees forest or The forest where parrot trees grow.
kisukavaṇṇa: Kiṃ sukavaṇṇa(ti) [kiṃ suka+vaṇṇa] The appearance is like a parrot flower.
kisukicca: Kiṃ Sukicca (na) [kiṃ su+kicca] What function or what matter.
kisukopamadīpita: Kiṃ sukopamadīpita(ti) [kiṃ sukopamā+dīpita] A simile of a parrot tree.
kisukopamā: Kiṃ sukopamā(thī) [kiṃ suka+upamā] A simile of a parrot tree.
kisukāriṭṭha: Kiṃ sukāriṭṭha(pu) [kiṃsuka+ariṭṭha] The medicine that is made of the solution of parrot wood. The medicine that is made with the dissolution of the ash of the parrot wood.
kisusayojana: Kiṃ susaṃyojana(ti) [kiṃsu+saṃyojana] One who has which attachment.
kisuviya: Kiṃ Suviya (bya) How? As it is shameful. As it is miserable. See - Kismiṃviya.
kisāra: Kiṃ sāra(ti) [kiṃ+sāra] Which is the essence?
kisīla: Kiṃ sīla(ti) [kiṃ+sīla] One who observes which rules of conduct.
kiuttara: Kin Ottara (Ti) [Kin + Ottara] Which dhamma is superior.
kivata: Kiṃ vata(pu,na) [kiṃ+vata] (1) What kinds of virtues. One who observes which rules of conduct.
kivedana: Kiṃ Vedana (ti) [kiṃ+vedanā] What pain is he suffering from or does he suffer which kind of pain or disease.
kivāda: Kiṃ vāda(pu) [kiṃ+vāda] What kind of doctrine or taking which doctrine. See - Kiṃ vādī.
kivādī: Kiṃ vādī(ti) [kiṃ+vada+ṇī. Kiṃ vāda+ī. Kiṃ vadati sīlenāti kiṃ vādī. Atha vā ko katamo vādo kiṃ vādo, so etassa atthīti kiṃ vādī. Sārattha, 1. 142.] One who takes or believes which doctrine.
kiākāra: Kiṃ ākāra(pu) [kiṃ+ākāra] What nature of thing or what state of affairs. See - Kiṃpaṭibhāga.
kikiṇī: [Kiṃ+kaṇa+a+ī] (thī) CL=7 [Kiṃ kucchitaṃ kaṇatīti kiṃkaṇī, nadādi. Kiṃ kiṇītipi pāṭhantaraṃ, tadā yadādi. Dhāna, ṭī. 286. Kaṇa+a+ī. Kaṇa-itidaṇḍako dhātu saddattho. Tassa dvittaṃ assa ittaṃ niggahītāgamoca. Sūci.] The tinkling bell. Small bells. See also - Kiṅkiṇikā.
